data.text: Hannah prayed and said, “My heart exults in the LORD; my horn is lifted high in the LORD. My mouth is opened wide against my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation.
There is none holy like the LORD, for there is none besides you; there is no rock like our God.
Do not keep speaking so proudly; let no arrogance come from your mouth. For the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
The bows of mighty warriors are broken, but those who stumbled have girded themselves with strength.
Those who were full hire themselves out for bread, but those who were hungry hunger no more. The barren woman has borne seven, but she who had many sons has withered.
The LORD puts to death and gives life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.
The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and also exalts.

He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap, to seat them with nobles and give them a throne of honor as their inheritance. For the pillars of the earth are the LORD’s, and he has set the world upon them.
He guards the feet of his faithful ones, but the wicked are silenced in darkness, for a man does not prevail by strength.

The LORD’s adversaries will be shattered; he will thunder against them from heaven. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth. He will give strength to his king and lift high the horn of his anointed.”
Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy ministered to the LORD before Eli the priest.
Eli’s sons were worthless men; they did not know the LORD.
data.titulo: Eli's Sons Treat the Offering With Contempt

data.text: This was the priests’ custom with the people: whenever anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest’s servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fork in his hand.

He would thrust it into the basin, kettle, cauldron, or cooking pot. Whatever the fork brought up, the priest would take for himself. This is what they did to all the Israelites who came there to Shiloh.
Even before they burned the fat, the priest’s servant would come and say to the man offering the sacrifice, “Give the priest meat to roast, for he will not accept boiled meat from you, only raw.”
If the man said to him, “Let them first burn the fat, then take as much as you desire,” he would say, “No, you must give it now. If not, I will take it by force.”
The sin of the young men was very great before the LORD, for the men treated the LORD’s offering with contempt.
But Samuel ministered before the LORD, a boy wearing a linen ephod.
data.titulo: Samuel's Service and Hannah's Growing Household

data.text: His mother would make him a little robe and bring it to him year after year when she went up with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.
Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife and say, “May the LORD give you offspring by this woman in place of what was asked of the LORD.” Then they would go back to their own place.
The LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. The boy Samuel grew up in the LORD’s presence.
Now Eli was very old. He heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and that they were sleeping with the women who served at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
He said to them, “Why do you do such things? I hear of your evil deeds from all these people.
No, my sons. The report I hear the LORD’s people spreading is not good.

If a man sins against another, God will mediate for him. But if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?” Yet they did not listen to their father’s voice, for the LORD desired to put them to death.
The boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with both the LORD and people.
A man of God came to Eli and said to him, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Did I not clearly reveal myself to your father’s house when they were in Egypt, in Pharaoh’s house?
data.titulo: The LORD's Word Against Eli's House

data.text: I chose him from all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod before me. I gave your father’s house all the offerings by fire of the Israelites.
Why do you kick at my sacrifice and my offering, which I commanded for my dwelling? You honor your sons more than me, fattening yourselves on the best of every offering of my people Israel.

Therefore the LORD, the God of Israel, declares: I did indeed say that your house and your father’s house would walk before me forever. But now the LORD declares: Far be it from me! I will honor those who honor me, but those who despise me will be lightly esteemed.
The days are coming when I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father’s house, so that there will be no old man in your house.
You will see distress in my dwelling, even amid all the good done for Israel, and there will never be an old man in your house.
Any man of yours whom I do not cut off from my altar will be left to wear out your eyes and grieve your soul, and all the descendants of your house will die as grown men.
This will be the sign for you that will come upon your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: both of them will die on the same day.
I will raise up for myself a faithful priest who will do what is in my heart and in my soul. I will build him a faithful house, and he will always walk before my anointed.
data.titulo: The Promise of a Faithful Priest

data.text: Everyone left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, “Please assign me to one of the priestly duties, so that I may eat a piece of bread.”’”
